title: Paying for Information, Not for Clicks: A Block-Level Publisher Content Marketplace for AI Answers
abstract: arXiv:2610.30324v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We propose a publisher content marketplace that allocates payments for information used in AI-generated answers. The unit of attribution is a ``lego block:'' a distinct fact or piece of commentary that may appear in articles from multiple publishers. A simple news-reading model connects three payment rules: equal sharing among all publishers reporting on a block, rewarding the publisher who reported a block first, and rewarding indispensable contributions. Each can be represented within a Shapley-value framework.   We evaluate the framework using answers to 1,974 search-engine queries about a heavily covered news episode. When attribution considers only the articles retrieved for an individual query, most cited blocks appear unique, and the rules produce nearly identical allocations. A global index covering the full news corpus reveals overlap across publishers, making the choice of payment rule consequential. Premium publishers, defined

translated_title: 为信息付费，而非为点击付费：面向AI答案的区块级出版商内容市场
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一个出版商内容市场，为AI生成答案中所使用的信息分配支付报酬。归因的基本单位是“乐高块”：一个独特的事实或评论片段，可能出现在多个出版商的文章中。一个简单的新闻阅读模型连接了三种支付规则：在报道同一块内容的所有出版商之间平均分摊、奖励最先报道某块内容的出版商、以及奖励不可或缺的贡献。每一种规则都可以在Shapley值框架内表示。我们使用针对某个被大量报道新闻事件的1,974个搜索引擎查询的答案来评估该框架。当归因仅考虑为单个查询检索到的文章时，大多数被引用的块看起来是独特的，各规则产生几乎相同的分配结果。而覆盖完整新闻语料库的全局索引则揭示了出版商之间的内容重叠，使得支付规则的选择变得至关重要。
tldr: 该论文提出一种以“乐高块”（独特事实或评论片段）为归因单位的出版商内容市场，在Shapley值框架下比较平均分摊、首发奖励和不可或缺贡献三种支付规则，为AI答案中使用的信息向出版商分配报酬。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a block-level publisher content marketplace that pays for information used in AI answers, attributing value to "lego blocks" (distinct facts or commentary) and comparing three Shapley-value-based payment rules: equal sharing, first-reporter rewards, and rewards for indispensable contributions.
